scores.evidence: returns 202 within 10 s (GitHub's webhook timeout)... Verifies the `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC
scores.rationale: GitHub webhook semantics, App permission model (no `workflows` permission blocking CI changes), installation tokens, delivery-ID idempotency and microVM isolation are all stated accurately, including the subtle guarantees the design depends on.

scores.evidence: reads new issues and triages them... reproduces the bug, writes a fix in a sandbox, and opens a **draft PR**
scores.rationale: Covers both triage and resolution exactly as asked, resolves autonomy ambiguity with explicit tiers, and every exclusion (auto-merge, auto-close, multi-provider) is deferred with a stated trigger.

scores.evidence: A separate executor holds the GitHub token, checks each action against policy, and runs it.
scores.rationale: Ledger ownership, token custody, policy enforcement and the sandbox boundary are decided once and honored consistently in every phase and cross-cutting table, with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: Thresholds are starting targets; recalibrate once a baseline exists.
scores.rationale: Each phase has checkable exit criteria, the riskiest assumptions (injection, sandbox reproducibility, resolve rate) are tested early via red-team suite, replay harness and shadow mode, thresholds are labeled provisional, and validation continues in production via scorecards.

scores.evidence: Assumptions (none were given): GitHub.com, one org... If any of these is wrong, re-check gates G1, G6 and G7.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit up front, every default decision carries a revisit trigger explaining what changes if it proves wrong, and numeric targets are marked as provisional rather than asserted facts.

scores.evidence: An attacker hides instructions in an issue body, a code comment or test output.
scores.rationale: Covers injection, memory/eval poisoning, duplicate deliveries, half-finished actions (reconciler), flaky tests, provider outage and runaway loops with concrete detection and recovery; only human/agent collision on in-flight issues is thin.

scores.evidence: Alerts fire when dead-letter-queue depth is above 0, job error rate is above 5% over 15 minutes
scores.rationale: Deployment, meaningful alerts, kill switches and per-repo isolation are concrete and sized to a small team, but incident ownership/on-call and explicit deployment rollback are not specified.

scores.evidence: Per-repo daily cap and an org-wide monthly cap. Reaching a cap pauses the repo's queue and alerts.
scores.rationale: The dominant driver (model inference) has per-task budgets, caps, tiering and tracked cost-per-resolved-issue, and build-vs-buy is cost-framed, but engineering/build cost and overall run-cost magnitude are never estimated.

scores.evidence: The ledger and policy schema already key on `(provider, org, repo)` to keep this open
scores.rationale: A decision table separates defaults from revisit triggers, hard-to-reverse items (ledger schema, model coupling, autonomy expansion) get isolation or exit paths, and reversible choices are made quickly without over-analysis.

scores.evidence: **Postgres-backed queue**... This allows transactional enqueue and is the simplest option.
scores.rationale: Modular monolith, single agent loop, no fine-tuning or embedding index until triggers fire — every component is justified by a need and the only forced split is a security boundary.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 — First end-to-end slice... within 60 s, the agent posts a comment
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: concrete first slice, dependency-justified phase ordering, specific technology and schema decisions, checkable exit criteria per phase, and deferral conditions that say how to adapt.

checklist.evidence: **Forbidden:** merge, close, push to the default branch, workflow or settings changes.
GitHub App with fine-grained, per-repo installations... **No `workflows` permission**... Short-lived installation tokens.
The model can only **propose** typed actions; the executor checks each one against policy.
an ephemeral microVM per job. No secrets. Network egress denied except a proxy that allows only package registries
The body contains the reproduction, root-cause summary, test evidence, trace link and an "AI-generated" label.
offline type-label accuracy ≥ 85% top-1. Duplicate precision ≥ 90% at recall ≥ 50%. Two weeks of shadow mode
Outcome capture schema: human label edits after agent labels, PR merged / merged-with-edits / closed, review comments.
a single feature flag that stops all GitHub writes. It exists from commit one.
Triage: ≤ 30k input tokens, ≤ $0.05... Resolution: ≤ 40 tool iterations, ≤ $3 per attempt
full job replay possible from ledger (inputs, model version, prompt hash)
agentic search tools inside the sandbox (`ripgrep`, tree-sitter symbol lookup, file reads)
inserts the event into Postgres keyed by `X-GitHub-Delivery`. Duplicate deliveries do nothing.

traps.evidence: The agent never merges, never closes issues and never pushes to default branches. PRs are drafts only.
The token never enters model context or the sandbox.
treat as untrusted data: issue titles, bodies, comments, repo files (README, code comments), test output
replay resolve rate ≥ 20% (hidden tests pass) and **zero** proposed PRs with failing visible tests
a deliberately looping test task is cut off at the iteration cap

note: An exceptionally strong plan that avoids every trap and concretely addresses nearly the whole domain checklist; remaining gaps are human/agent coordination on in-flight issues, incident ownership, and build-cost estimation.
